headline: A 2014 law lets the Treasury mint $1 silver coins in 2018 to mark the centennial of America's entry into World War I.
what_it_does: The law directs the Treasury Secretary to mint and issue $1 silver coins only during 2018 to commemorate the World War I centennial. It also requires a juried design competition, with a paid prize for the winning design. Each coin sold carries a $10 surcharge paid to the United States Foundation for the Commemoration of the World Wars to support the World War I Centennial Commission. The Treasury must ensure the program has no net cost to the government and must recover its design and issuing costs before any surcharge money goes out.
when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 16, 2014; coins may be issued only during calendar year 2018.
